card.done: Families basic to complex, validation mae mean ± SE over the folds: dummy 6.4946 ± 0.6889 days; linear/logistic 5.4701 ± 0.6733 days; single tree 5.4244 ± 0.7147 days; forest 5.4434 ± 0.6826 days. Ladder: linear/logistic kept over dummy; single tree not kept over linear/logistic; forest not kept over linear/logistic. One-SE choice over all four: linear/logistic (best mean: single tree).
card.observation: Paired per-fold gain of each step (positive = the more complex family is better; description only, s01 1.7): linear/logistic vs dummy +1.0245 days (paired SE 0.1262), better in 5 of 5 folds; single tree vs linear/logistic +0.0458 days (paired SE 0.0685), better in 3 of 5 folds; forest vs linear/logistic +0.0267 days (paired SE 0.0601), better in 3 of 5 folds.
card.reasoning: A more complex family is adopted only when its gain over the current family clears one standard error of the fold means (the agreed rule). The fold SE also carries the level differences between folds (drift), so a small but consistent paired gain can stay below it; the paired figures show that without changing the decision.
card.conclusion: These are selection scores on the folds, not generalisation estimates (G-10). s07 tunes the linear and tree families and compares each tuned configuration with its plain s06 model (G-55).
card.label: observation
